classification.difficultyReason: Requires an absolute-value reflection before adding ordinates to an unscaled straight-line graph.

spec.description: Unscaled coordinate axes, an increasing blue S-shaped curve and a rising red straight line through their intersection. Two unlabelled dashed horizontal asymptotes, continuation arrows and coloured series labels are retained.
spec.mathematics: The drawing coordinates are schematic placement coordinates only. No equation, numerical scale, slope or asymptote value is asserted for the supplied graphs.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graphs only; the requested transformed graph is absent.

answer.short:
The graph passes through the axes' intersection. For $x<0$, use $y=g(x)-f(x)$; for $x\geq0$, use $y=g(x)+f(x)$.

Reflect the negative part of $f$ in the $x$-axis, then add its ordinates to those of $g$.
answer.worked:
Reflect the part of $y=f(x)$ below the $x$-axis to obtain $y=|f(x)|$. Add the ordinates of this graph and $y=g(x)$ at each $x$.

$$y=\begin{cases}g(x)-f(x),&x<0,\\g(x)+f(x),&x\geq0.\end{cases}$$

The left branch lies above $g$, and the right branch lies above both supplied graphs. Both branches meet at the axes' intersection.

spec.description: A solid transformed curve with the supplied f and g retained as faint dashed construction graphs.
spec.mathematics: On the left, the supplied Bezier ordinates are subtracted from the straight-line ordinates; on the right they are added. This preserves the qualitative source geometry without assigning an equation to f.
